title: Resampling schemes and the sampling-unit contract

items.title: Sampling units and the resampling-unit contract
items.statement: Define the indivisible random or design unit in the declared experiment and require resampling at a unit level that preserves dependence relevant to the declared target.

items.title: Empirical measure of observed units
items.statement: For a nonempty observed tuple in a measurable unit space, define its empirical measure as the equally weighted sum of its Dirac measures, counting repeated observations with multiplicity.

items.title: Uniform laws on finite subset families
items.statement: For 0 <= r <= n, the family of r-element subsets of [n] is finite and nonempty, and equal weights define a probability law on it, including r=0 and r=n.

items.title: The empirical measure is a probability measure
items.statement: For every nonempty finite observed tuple in a measurable space, its empirical measure is a probability measure.

items.title: Delete-d jackknife replicates and their uniform average
items.statement: For 1 <= d < n, compute a declared measurable statistic on each complement of a d-subset of the observed sampling-unit indices and return the replicates and their uniform average; no variance scaling is implicit.

items.title: Uniform subsampling without replacement
items.statement: For 1 <= b < n, select a uniformly distributed b-subset of observed sampling-unit indices without replacement and apply the declared measurable size-b statistic.

items.title: Size-n bootstrap from the empirical law
items.statement: For n >= 1, draw n sampling units conditionally IID from the empirical probability measure of the observed units and apply the declared size-n statistic.

items.title: Empirical-law bootstrap draws are conditionally IID
items.statement: Conditional on a fixed observed tuple of n >= 1 units, the size-n bootstrap sample has joint law equal to the n-fold product of the empirical law, hence its entries are IID from that empirical law.

title: Resampling schemes and the sampling-unit contract — Examples

items.title: The bootstrap law of a two-point sample mean
items.statement: For observed IID real units (0,2), compute exactly the conditional size-two bootstrap distribution of the sample mean without asserting its asymptotic validity.

items.title: Delete-d replicates and subsampling on four units
items.statement: On four observed real units, calculate all delete-two means and distinguish their uniform average from a variance estimate, then compare the uniform size-two subsampling law and identify its equality with the delete-two replicate law under complementation for the sample mean.

items.title: Resampling complete cluster records
items.statement: Treat each observed cluster vector as one unit and resample whole vectors, preserving each vector's within-cluster records in every replicate.

items.title: Pointwise bootstrap need not preserve pair dependence
items.statement: Refute the claim that the conditional pointwise bootstrap reproduces the joint sampling law for every dependent pair by comparing their pairwise covariances in a finite binary model.

items.title: Assignment randomization and bootstrap are different laws
items.statement: For a two-unit Fisher-sharp-null design, calculate the known assignment-randomization law and contrast it with the empirical bootstrap law on observed outcomes.
